A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ReCamDriving and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary material. The formatting and appendix organization differ, but corresponding content can be reliably matched.

before.justification: V1 reports original WOD and NuScenes evaluations, quantitative ablations, and qualitative novel-trajectory generation results in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: V3 retains the original benchmark evaluations and ablations and additionally reports temporal-consistency scores and qualitative experiments using STORM renderings.

M1.justification: Sections 3–4 retain the same cross-trajectory data construction, pose-conditioned first stage, frozen first-stage parameters, rendering and cross-attention modules, and flow-matching objective. STORM supplies alternative conditioning renderings for an additional evaluation; no new ReCamDriving component or training procedure is introduced.

E1.justification: WOD, NuScenes, and lateral-trajectory synthesis remain the coverage. V3 Section 10 adds an input-condition scenario using lower-quality feed-forward STORM renderings, extending evaluation beyond the optimized DriveStudio guidance used in v1.

E2.justification: The WOD comparisons retain DriveStudio, Difix3D+, FreeVS, and StreetCrafter; NuScenes retains DriveStudio and Difix3D+. Existing ablation comparators also remain. STORM is a conditioning provider rather than an added competing synthesis method. The expanded repair-baseline description does not establish that the baseline changed.

E3.justification: V3 replaces adjacent-frame CLIP similarity, CLIP-F, with optical-flow Temporal Consistency Error in the benchmark and repair-baseline comparisons. Its additional STORM test constructs 121-frame conditions by rolling out and concatenating 20-frame segments. Existing evaluation scenes, lateral offsets, training budgets, resolution, and video length remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V3 Section 10 and Figure 11 add a qualitative robustness test using STORM guidance. Section 12 and Figure 12 add stage-one versus stage-two examples at ±4 m, extending the pose-only versus rendering-conditioned analysis already present in v1. The existing ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for its experiments. V3's temporal averaging defines an evaluation metric rather than introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: CLIP-F entries are replaced by TCE results in v3 Tables 1, 3, and 5; for example, ReCamDriving reports TCE 3.38 at WOD ±1 m and 3.79 on NuScenes. These are different metrics, not same-setting performance gains. Shared IQ, camera-error, FID, FVD, and CLIP-V values remain unchanged. STORM and additional stage-comparison qualitative results are added.

T1.justification: V3 Section 11 introduces the mathematical definition of the newly adopted TCE metric through forward-backward flow reprojection error and temporal averaging in Equation 6. The method's flow-matching and latent-conditioning Equations 1–5 remain unchanged; no new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a LiDAR-free, two-stage camera-controlled generation framework, scalable cross-trajectory supervision through ParaDrive, and state-of-the-art camera controllability and structural consistency. Rewording emphasizes lateral supervision already central to v1 without materially changing these contributions.

C2.justification: V3 expands the geometric-alignment explanation for two-stage training and interprets source-input sensitivity as evidence against mere artifact repair. Sections 6 and 10 discuss reconstruction overhead and feed-forward compatibility. V1's explicit limitation concerning small distant objects is removed, without evidence that this failure condition was resolved.

D1.justification: V3 documents SEA-RAFT, center-cropped point sampling, and forward-backward checking for TCE, plus the STORM segment-rollout procedure. It also explicitly states that the repair baseline omits camera-pose injection, supplementing v1's description. Existing hardware, training hyperparameters, dataset identifiers, and resource-access statements are retained.

R1.justification: V3 adds references supporting feed-forward reconstruction, temporal evaluation, and identity/content-consistent generation, including DGGT, STORM, WorldScore, and SEA-RAFT. It replaces v1's mismatched FreeSim freeway-simulator reference with the driving-view synthesis work. The central positioning against repair-based and LiDAR-conditioned approaches remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are reworked, several method and ablation explanations are expanded, and ParaDrive terminology is corrected. Discussion is separated from the conclusion, and supplementary sections are expanded and renumbered. The main method/experiment sequence and substantial passages remain intact.

P2.justification: The paper is extensively reformatted from two columns to one. Figure 2 is redrawn, qualitative panels and input/output labels are reorganized, and camera-error columns become a separate table. Two supplementary figures are added; v1 Figures 11–12 are retained as v3 Figures 13–14. These constitute substantial display and layout changes.

improvement.justification: The STORM compatibility experiment, additional stage comparisons, and explicit temporal-metric and repair-baseline procedures modestly strengthen empirical support and assessability. Clearer figure labeling and the corrected FreeSim reference also help. These benefits are tempered by removal of the distant-object limitation and discussion of hours-to-seconds reconstruction savings without measured runtime evidence. The gains are incremental because the core method and shared quantitative findings remain unchanged.
